summary: Backend-only audit of Sign in with Apple (POST /api/auth/apple). 14/14 pytest cases pass in-process (httpx.ASGITransport) with a locally-minted RS256 JWT signed by a keypair injected into services.apple_auth._JWKS_CACHE. Covers: malformed token, happy-path new user, idempotent second call keyed on apple_sub, wrong audience, wrong issuer, expired token, missing sub, legacy email/password->Apple linking, private-relay (no email) synthetic user, APPLE_AUDIENCES-missing env, sparse-unique apple_sub index presence, register+login+/me regression, google-session endpoint reachable, and new Apple user is_instructor=false. Public preview URL smoke-tested for the malformed path (returns 401 'Malformed token' as expected). Frontend not tested per request scope (native-only Apple button).
critical_code_review_comments: services/apple_auth.py: verify_identity_token correctly enforces iss/aud/exp/iat/sub/aud/iss required claims and fails closed if APPLE_AUDIENCES is not set — good security posture.
routes/auth.py apple_sign_in: three-tier lookup (apple_sub -> email -> new) is correct; apple_sub is stamped on the linked user immediately so subsequent sign-ins hit the fast path.
Legacy linking preserves password_hash (verified by test_legacy_linking_by_email) — an existing email/password user can add Apple without losing password login.
Private-relay path uses `apple:<sub>` synthetic email + email_is_synthetic=true flag — correct and does not collide with a real address because ':' is invalid in real emails.
startup._ensure_indexes creates users.apple_sub as unique+sparse — verified via test_apple_sub_index_exists.
Nit (out of scope): server.py still uses @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown'), which FastAPI deprecates in favour of lifespan handlers — non-blocking but shows up as warnings in every test run.

Nit (out of scope): AppleTokenError message for bogus tokens leaks the underlying jwt exception detail ('Invalid header string: ...utf-8 codec...'). Not a security issue but consider clamping to just 'Malformed token' in production for cleaner client UX.
seed_data_creation: All test users are created with TEST_ prefix and hard-deleted in per-test finally blocks. No residual data in db.users, db.follows, or db.activity_events.
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini (asyncio_default_*_loop_scope=session) is required because Motor's client is bound to a single event loop. If you add more async DB-touching tests, run them under this same config (`pytest -c /app/backend/tests/pytest.ini`). Apple JWKS is mocked by writing directly into services.apple_auth._JWKS_CACHE — never hits the real Apple URL during tests. Real Apple sign-in can only be exercised on an iOS device build; the frontend button is Platform.OS==='ios' gated.
